item.title: China social media thrashes one-child policy after population control czar dies
item.description: The death of former one-child policy head Peng Peiyun sparked social media criticism, with users lamenting the policy's impact on lost children and China's declining population. While state media praised her work, netizens blamed the policy for demographic challenges, including a shrinking workforce and increased elderly care costs.

item.title: A million more Epstein documents have been found, justice department says
item.description: The Justice Department has discovered over 1 million additional documents potentially linked to the Jeffrey Epstein investigation, significantly increasing the volume of material to be released. This discovery will extend the timeline for disclosure, with a full release now expected in a few more weeks.

item.title: In first Christmas sermon, Pope Leo tells world’s leaders to talk rather than make war
item.description: Pope Leo XIV, in his inaugural Christmas message, implored for global peace, urging an end to wars, injustice, and persecution. He championed the cause of refugees, climate disaster victims, and the unemployed, echoing his predecessor's concerns. The pontiff stressed personal responsibility and dialogue, particularly in Latin America and Europe amidst ongoing conflicts.

item.title: Bangladesh: After Dipu Chandra Das, another Hindu man lynched
item.description: A Hindu man, Amrit Mandal, was beaten to death in Bangladesh on charges of extortion. Officials stated Mandal was a known criminal leading a gang involved in terrorist activities and extortion. He was reportedly killed by an angry mob after attempting to extort money and assaulting a local's son.

item.title: Tarique Rahman's return: Exiled BNP leader gets rousing welcome; vows inclusive Bangladesh
item.description: Tarique Rahman, son of former PM Khaleda Zia, returned to Bangladesh after 17 years, drawing parallels between 1971 and 2024's political upheaval. Addressing thousands, he pledged to build an inclusive, safe nation, stating, "I have a plan" for the country's development and vowing to maintain peace. His return aims to energize supporters for upcoming elections.

item.title: ‘Viciously killing innocent Christians’: Trump orders deadly strikes on ISIS targets in Nigeria
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced a "powerful and deadly strike" against ISIS terrorists in northwest Nigeria, citing their targeting and killing of Christians. He claimed the "Department of War" executed "perfect strikes" at his direction, vowing to prevent radical Islamic terrorism from prospering. Trump had previously warned of repercussions if the slaughter of Christians continued.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: More than medicine: How a weight-loss drug helped US envoy free prisoners in Belarus
item.description: A casual chat about weight loss between a US envoy and Belarus's leader, Alexander Lukashenko, unexpectedly paved the way for releasing over 120 political prisoners. The personal exchange, involving a prescription drug, helped break the ice for crucial negotiations on sanctions relief and prisoner swaps, ultimately reuniting families and easing US restrictions on key Belarusian exports.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Dipu Chandra Das, say his name’: Laura Loomer attacks Islamic hatred after lynching of Hindu man in Bangladesh
item.description: A Hindu factory worker, Dipu Chandra Das, was lynched in Bangladesh following unverified blasphemy accusations. Right-wing activist Laura Loomer highlighted the incident, warning of spreading Islamist hatred and urging international attention. The killing has reignited concerns for religious minorities in Bangladesh, with critics questioning the current leadership's response to such attacks.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: YouTuber Cleetus McFarland goes viral after gifting his employees $3,000 mini jeeps for Christmas
item.description: Automotive YouTuber Cleetus McFarland surprised his employees with a unique Christmas bonus, gifting around 20 staff members Massimo Mini 125 mini jeeps valued at $3,000 each. This festive gesture, captured in a viral video, aligns perfectly with his high-octane brand and creative approach to employee appreciation, continuing a tradition of fun, vehicle-based rewards.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Candace Owens faces pushback as Alex Jones questions her Charlie Kirk claims after Laura Loomer talks
item.description: Laura Loomer says she helped Alex Jones change his stance on Candace Owens after Owens shared unproven claims about Charlie Kirk’s killing. Jones later challenged Owens on InfoWars, questioned her eyewitness source, and said innocent people were being accused. Owens defended her reporting, while Erika Kirk has stayed silent publicly so far.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: ‘We did nothing wrong’: Indian truck drivers challenge California over mass licence cancellations
item.description: Thousands of Indian truck drivers in California are suing the state after their commercial licenses were slated for cancellation due to federal audit findings on expiry dates. Drivers, many of whom are Punjabi Sikhs, argue the state's errors are punishing them and threatening their livelihoods and families. Advocacy groups warn of increased profiling and wider economic disruption.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Talibanisation of Bangladesh': Awami League student wing chief flags Yunus govt's role in minority persecution; fanning anti-India rhetoric
item.description: Bangladesh Students League president Saddam Hussain accused the interim government and its leader Muhammad Yunus of encouraging anti-India rhetoric to appease extremist groups and cover up governance failures. He also criticised the return of BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman, calling it a backdoor deal that could deepen political polarisation and undermine democracy. The developments come amid continued mob killings, political unrest and heightened concerns over minority safety and law and order ahead of the February 17 general elections.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Candace Owens sparks outrage after encouraging Ben Shapiro to take his own life during public feud
item.description: Candace Owens and Ben Shapiro's public fallout has escalated into a bitter war of words, intensifying scrutiny within conservative media. The dispute, stemming from disagreements over politics and foreign policy, has now moved into deeply personal territory, with Owens making shocking remarks about Shapiro following his criticism of her conspiracy theories.
item.dc:creator: Barsha Dutta

item.title: Kick bans streamer Braden “Clavicular” after shocking Tesla Cybertruck incident caught on live stream where he allegedly “killed” a man
item.description: Online streamer Braden “Clavicular” was reportedly banned from the streaming platform Kick after a livestream showed him allegedly running over a person with a Tesla Cybertruck. Clavicular claimed he acted in self-defense, fearing for his safety as people surrounded his vehicle. The condition of the individual and official details remain unclear.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Adin Ross net worth in 2025: Kick earnings, cars, mansion, and investment portfolio
item.description: Adin Ross, a popular 25-year-old streamer, has amassed an estimated $24 million net worth by 2025. His primary income stems from lucrative Kick streaming deals, supplemented by investments in real estate, luxury cars, stocks, bonds, cryptocurrency, and NFTs. Ross's success highlights how talent and strategic moves can transform online fame into significant wealth.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: TikTok star Tea Tyme arrested after fatal livestream driving crash kills 59 year old pedestrian
item.description: TikTok creator Tynesha McCarty-Wroten, known as Tea Tyme, has been arrested for reckless homicide and aggravated use of a communication device resulting in death. Police allege she was livestreaming on November 3 when she fatally struck a pedestrian in a Chicago suburb. The incident, captured on video, sparked public outrage, especially after McCarty-Wroten later solicited donations online.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: What is Charlie Kirk’s final book? Podcaster Mary Katharine Ham speaks out as Erika Kirk is questioned for public grieving
item.description: Charlie Kirk’s final book was released after his death in September 2025. His widow, Erika Kirk, faced backlash for promoting it so soon. Journalist Mary Katharine Ham defended her, saying grief has no set path. Erika Kirk says continuing her husband’s work helps her heal and keeps his vision alive.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: “People look at me as a joke”: Kai Cenat responds to online mockery with a firm message about vulnerability and mental health
item.description: Twitch star Kai Cenat bravely opened up about self-doubt and mental strain, facing both support and ridicule. He clarified his intention was to foster mental health conversations, not to claim depression. Cenat highlighted how negative feedback revealed why many remain silent, emphasizing the importance of speaking up despite potential mockery, finding inspiration in anime like Naruto.
item.dc:creator: Barsha Dutta

item.title: Explained: How Americans misused the J-1 visa and exploited foreign labour
item.description: The J-1 visa allows foreign students, interns and trainees to work temporarily in the US under categories such as summer work travel, internships and professional training. While the programme sits under the US State Department, its day-to-day functioning is outsourced to more than a hundred approved sponsor organisations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bangladesh unrest: Another Hindu man lynched; cops link it to extortion bid
item.description: Bangladesh faces renewed criticism after a second lynching, this time of Amrit Mondal, just days after worker Dipu Chandra Das was killed. Mondal was allegedly beaten to death by villagers after demanding extortion money. These incidents highlight growing concerns over the safety of minority communities amidst ongoing unrest.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
